L67@P2: A Revision history 58
L68@P2-3: 31 Introduction and design rationale
L69@P3: This submission defines a family of key-encapsulation mechanisms (KEMs), collectively called FrodoKEM.
L70@P3: The FrodoKEM schemes are designed to be conservative yet practical post-quantum constructions whose
L71@P3: security derives from cautious parameterizations of the well-studied learning with errors problem, which in
L72@P3: turn has close connections to conjectured-hard problems on generic, “algebraically unstructured” lattices.
L73@P3: Concretely, FrodoKEM is designed for IND-CCA security at three levels:
L74@P3: • FrodoKEM-640, which targets Level 1 in the NIST call for proposals (matching or exceeding the
L75@P3: brute-force security of AES-128), and
L76@P3: • FrodoKEM-976, which targets Level 3 in the NIST call for proposals (matching or exceeding the
L77@P3: brute-force security of AES-192).
L78@P3: • FrodoKEM-1344, which targets Level 5 in the NIST call for proposals (matching or exceeding the
L79@P3: brute-force security of AES-256).
L80@P3: Two variants of each of the above schemes are provided:
L81@P3: • FrodoKEM-640-AES, FrodoKEM-976-AES, and FrodoKEM-1344-AES, which use AES128 to pseudorandomly generate a large public matrix (called A).
L82@P3: • FrodoKEM-640-SHAKE, FrodoKEM-976-SHAKE, and FrodoKEM-1344-SHAKE, which use SHAKE128
L83@P3: to pseudorandomly generate the matrix.
L84@P3: The AES variants are particularly suitable for devices having AES hardware acceleration (such as AES-NI
L85@P3: on Intel platforms), while the SHAKE variants generally provide competitive or better performance in
L86@P3: comparison with the AES variants in the absence of hardware acceleration.
L87@P3: In the remainder of this section, we outline FrodoKEM’s scientific lineage, briefly explain our design choices
L88@P3: (with further details appearing in subsequent sections), and describe other features of our proposal beyond
L89@P3: those explicitly requested by NIST.
L90@P3: Appendix A describes the changes/tweaks since the initial Round 1 submission to NIST.
L91@P3: 1.1 Pedigree
L92@P3: The core of FrodoKEM is a public-key encryption scheme called FrodoPKE,
L93@P3: 1 whose IND-CPA security is tightly
L94@P3: related to the hardness of a corresponding learning with errors problem. Here we briefly recall the scientific
L95@P3: lineage of these systems. See the surveys [91, 115, 102] for further details.
